- Workload: mix of model variants: small contextual embedding & 13B assistant (for browsing) + fallback to a 70B long-context model for deep analysis. Typical prompt+response lengths: 2k tokens (short) and up to 64k tokens for long runs.
- Questions: what dedicated GPU pool do you recommend for this mix? How much does switching from FP16 -> 4-bit quantization save us for models and KV cache? Any tradeoffs we should call out for SLOs (latency/quality)?

Can you turn around a ballpark by EOD Friday? Procurement would like line items for reserved capacity (monthly), burst headroom and a note on whether 64k context is feasible without excessive hardware.

Team / Emma — put together ballpark numbers and tradeoffs below. High-level takeaways up front:

1) 64k context is feasible but KV cache becomes the dominant memory consumer; model quantization reduces model footprint but has diminishing returns on total GPU memory when KV is large.
2) Recommend starting with a 6-node reserved pool (H100 80GB) for conservative baseline, with autoscale + burst to 8 nodes. Cost-optimized path uses A100 40GB with aggressive quantization + batching, but adds complexity and potential latency/quality degradation on long runs.

DETAILS
Assumptions:
- Long-run model: Llama-3-70B (baseline FP16); mid-run: 13B; small: 7B for embedding-like tasks.
- Typical request distribution: 70% short (<=2k tokens), 20% mid (2k-8k), 10% long (8k-64k). Peak concurrency: 50 concurrent long sessions (worst-case burst), or 150 mixed concurrent across all variants.
- KV cache per token estimate (model- and layer-dependent): ~0.0005 GB/token (this is conservative; actual varies by architecture / number of KV vectors stored). For planning, use 0.0005 GB/token across the 70B baseline.

Model sizes (approx):
- 70B FP16: ~140 GB (multi-GPU/sharded).
- 70B Q8: ~70 GB; 70B Q4: ~35 GB (single-GPU possible with 80GB devices if combined with KV offload strategies).
- 13B FP16: ~26 GB; Q4: ~6.5 GB.
- 7B FP16: ~14 GB; Q4: ~3.5 GB.

KV memory examples (per concurrent long request at 64k):
- 64k tokens * 0.0005 GB/token = 32 GB of KV per request for the 70B model.
- For 10 concurrent 64k sessions, KV = 320 GB (must be sharded across GPUs or offloaded to host memory).

Conservative (prod-ready) configuration — recommended for pilot with SLA:
- Hardware: 6 x H100 80GB reserved (pod-level abstraction).
- Placement: sharded model weights across 3 GPUs per 70B replica; KV shards distributed across remaining GPUs with local caching for active sessions.
- Concurrency planning: supports ~20 sustained long-context concurrent 64k sessions with headroom and 100 mixed short/mid sessions.
- Autoscale: burst to 8 nodes for large scheduled runs.
- Quantization: run 70B at Q4 where possible; keep mid/small variants at Q4. Use FP16 for immediate PoC only if quality concerns appear.
- Latency SLO: 95th percentile for long runs will be >1s (dominant by KV fetch + kernel prep); short requests should meet ~200-400ms depending on batching.

Cost-optimized configuration (lower monthly commitment):
- Hardware: 8 x A100 40GB with aggressive Q4 quantization + KV offload to host memory and prefix caching.
- Tradeoffs: higher engineering complexity to route long-context to specialized hosts, potential quality delta for Q4 on 70B, increased tail latency due to KV host-offload.

Operational notes / mitigations:
- Prefix/KV caching: cache common prefixes on-GPU to reduce repeated KV growth for short sessions.
- Model-variant routing: route user sessions by expected context length — short/mid to smaller models (13B/7B), only escalate to 70B for explicit deep analysis. This reduces KV pressure.
- Fallbacks: automatic degrade to 13B with prompt compression if KV budget is exhausted; maintain semantic equivalence tests so quality regressions are monitored.
- Monitoring: instrument token-level cost and per-request KV size; add regression alerts tied to eval prompt sets.

I'll attach the memory matrix with per-model per-quant estimates. Happy to tighten numbers if you can share expected distribution of long-run frequency (how often sessions hit the full 64k).

Emma — quick ops excerpt and a procurement-friendly summary for the MoM below. Happy to expand into a technical appendix.

Operations runbook excerpt (pilot):
- Reserved pool: 6 x H100 80GB as Marcus recommended. Owner: StratusAI account team.
- Autoscale triggers: +25% CPU/GPU utilization sustained for 3 minutes OR queue depth > 50 requests for 2 minutes -> scale +1 node. Manual scale to +2 nodes for scheduled batch analysis runs.
- Fallback policy: when KV per-GPU > 70% of available GPU RAM, route new long requests to 13B with prompt compression; flag degraded quality and notify Emma + Stratus SRE.
- Monitoring & alerts: token-cost per-request, p95 latency per model-variant, KV memory per-GPU. Monthly report to Stratus procurement with utilization and recommended commit adjustments.

Procurement-friendly summary (for MoM / PO):
- Baseline reserved: 6 x H100 (80GB) monthly commitment. Estimated monthly cost: [confidential — to be placed on official quote]. Burst: autoscale to 8 nodes during scheduled heavy analysis windows.
- Alternatives: 8 x A100 (40GB) with heavy quantization for cost-savings; requires extra integration work and may impact long-run latency.
